question: In which year did Anita Desai's novel, Clear Light of Day, make the Booker Prize shortlist?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1980**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anita Desai** is a renowned Indian author known for her profound works in English literature. Her novel **“Clear Light of Day”** is one of her most celebrated works.
 
• “Clear Light of Day” was shortlisted for the prestigious **Booker Prize** in the year **1980**, bringing international recognition to her literary prowess.
 
• The novel is set in Old Delhi and revolves around themes of family relationships, partition, and the passage of time.
 
• It is considered a semi-autobiographical work, reflecting Anita Desai’s own experiences growing up in India.
 
• The Booker Prize, established in **1969**, is one of the most prestigious awards in the literary world, given annually for the best original novel written in the English language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anita Desai’s Contributions:**

 
 
• Born on **24 June 1937** in Mussoorie, India, Anita Desai is a prominent figure in Indian English literature.
 
• She has been nominated for the **Booker Prize** multiple times, including for her novels “In Custody” (1984) and “Fasting, Feasting” (1999).
 
• Her works often explore themes of identity, cultural conflict, and the complexities of human relationships.
 
 
 
• **Clear Light of Day:**
 
 
• Published in **1980**, the novel is considered one of the finest examples of modern Indian literature in English.
 
• The story is set in the post-Partition era and focuses on the lives of the Das family.
 
• The novel is notable for its detailed portrayal of family dynamics and the psychological depth of its characters.
 
 
 
• **The Booker Prize:**
 
 
• Established in **1969**, the Booker Prize is awarded annually for the best original novel written in the English language and published in the UK or Ireland.
 
• Some of the notable winners of the prize include Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), and Margaret Atwood (2000).
 
• The award has significantly boosted the careers of many authors, including Anita Desai.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Clear Light of Day:**
 
 
• The novel is still studied in literary courses worldwide for its intricate narrative style and thematic richness.
 
• It has been praised for its vivid descriptions of Old Delhi and its deeply emotional exploration of the effects of time and memory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Works by Anita Desai:**

 
 
• **Cry, the Peacock (1963):** Her debut novel, which explores themes of mental illness and marital discord.
 
• **In Custody (1984):** A story about the struggle to preserve Urdu poetry, later adapted into a film.
 
• **Fasting, Feasting (1999):** A novel that contrasts the lives of siblings in India and the United States, also nominated for the Booker Prize.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Booker Prize:**
 
 
• Winning or being shortlisted for the Booker Prize often leads to international recognition and increased readership for authors.
 
• The prize focuses on literary excellence and has been instrumental in highlighting diverse voices in literature.
